nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a list over $\alpha$, let $k$ be a list over $\alpha$ extended by a fresh terminator symbol, and let $i$ be a natural number. If looking up $k$ in the suffix tree of $s$ returns $i$, then $i \le |s|$ and $k$ is the terminated string of $s$ with its first $i$ symbols removed.
nodes.title: Lookup in the suffix tree returns starting indices

nodes.summary: For lists $s$ and $p$ over $\alpha$, prefix search for $p$ (each symbol viewed in the alphabet extended by the terminator) in the suffix tree of $s$ succeeds if and only if there is a natural number $i$ such that $p$ is a prefix of the list obtained from $s$ by removing its first $i$ symbols.
nodes.title: Suffix-tree search finds exactly the prefixes of suffixes

nodes.summary: For lists $s$ and $p$ over $\alpha$, prefix search for $p$ (each symbol viewed in the alphabet extended by the terminator) in the suffix tree of $s$ succeeds if and only if $p$ occurs in $s$ as a contiguous sublist (an infix).
nodes.title: Suffix-tree search finds exactly the infixes

nodes.summary: For lists $s$ and $p$, $p$ is an infix (a contiguous sublist) of $s$ if and only if there is a natural number $i$ such that $p$ is a prefix of the list obtained from $s$ by removing its first $i$ symbols.
nodes.title: Infixes are prefixes of suffixes

nodes.summary: For lists $p$ and $q$ over $\alpha$, view their symbols in $\alpha$ extended by a fresh terminator symbol. If $p$ is a prefix of $q$ followed by the terminator, then $p$ is a prefix of $q$.
nodes.title: A tagged pattern cannot reach past the terminator

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a list over $\alpha$ and $i$ a natural number with $i \le |s|$. Looking up, in the suffix tree of $s$, the terminated string of $s$ with its first $i$ symbols removed returns $i$.
nodes.title: Lookup of a suffix returns its starting index

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a list over $\alpha$. A key $k$ is stored in the suffix tree of $s$ if and only if there is a natural number $i \le |s|$ such that $k$ is the terminated string of $s$ with its first $i$ symbols removed.
nodes.title: The stored keys of a suffix tree are its terminated suffixes

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a list over $\alpha$. The lists obtained from the terminated string of $s$ by removing its first $i$ symbols, for $i$ ranging over $0, 1, \ldots, |s|$, are pairwise distinct.
nodes.title: Terminated suffixes are distinct

nodes.summary: For a list $s$ over $\alpha$, the list of stored keys of the suffix tree of $s$ has length $|s| + 1$.
nodes.title: The suffix tree stores one key per suffix

nodes.summary: For a list $s$ over $\alpha$, the stored keys of $s$ form the list of keys stored in the suffix tree of $s$, in stored sibling order.
nodes.title: Stored keys of the suffix tree

nodes.summary: For a list $s = (s_0, \dots, s_{n-1})$ over $\alpha$, let $\hat s = (\mathrm{some}\,s_0, \dots, \mathrm{some}\,s_{n-1}, \mathrm{none})$ be its terminated string. The suffix entries of $s$ are the list of pairs $(\hat s_{\ge i}, i)$ for $i = 0, 1, \dots, n$ in increasing order, where $\hat s_{\ge i}$ is $\hat s$ with its first $i$ entries removed: each nonempty suffix of $\hat s$ paired with its starting index.
nodes.title: Suffix entries of a string

nodes.summary: For a list $s = (s_0, \dots, s_{n-1})$ over $\alpha$, let $\hat s = (\mathrm{some}\,s_0, \dots, \mathrm{some}\,s_{n-1}, \mathrm{none})$ be its terminated string over $\mathrm{Option}\,\alpha$. The suffix tree of $s$ is the radix trie with keys over $\mathrm{Option}\,\alpha$ and natural-number values obtained from the empty trie by inserting, for $i = n, n - 1, \dots, 0$ in this order, the suffix of $\hat s$…
nodes.title: Suffix tree

nodes.summary: For a list $s$ over $\alpha$ and a natural number $i \le |s|$, removing the first $i$ entries of the terminated string of $s$ gives the suffix of $s$ starting at index $i$ with every symbol tagged $\mathrm{some}$, followed by $\mathrm{none}$.
nodes.title: Suffixes of the terminated string

nodes.summary: For a list $s = (s_0, \dots, s_{n-1})$ over $\alpha$, the terminated string of $s$ is the list $(\mathrm{some}\,s_0, \dots, \mathrm{some}\,s_{n-1}, \mathrm{none})$ over $\mathrm{Option}\,\alpha$: every symbol of $s$ tagged $\mathrm{some}$, followed by the terminator $\mathrm{none}$.
nodes.title: Terminated string

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.

breadcrumbs.label: Tries, suffix structures and integer dictionaries
